title: Climate Adaptation Decisions and Public Evidence
learners: Policy students advising a fictional coastal municipality.
coursePurpose: Compare adaptation options using bounded evidence, distributional effects, uncertainty, and implementation constraints.
outcomes: Interpret an uncertainty range without converting it to certainty.
Compare options across effectiveness, equity, feasibility, and reversibility.
Write a decision memo with monitoring and revision triggers.

sourcePacket.content: Modeled annual flood loss in 2040 is 8-14 million fictional dollars under the stated scenario; the range is not a probability distribution.
Option A lowers modeled property loss but relocates twelve households. Option B has lower near-term protection and preserves residence, with a 2032 reassessment trigger.

customDeliverableDeclarations.name: Adaptation Decision Register
customDeliverableDeclarations.purpose: Let a policy team trace each adaptation decision to evidence, distributional effects, uncertainty, ownership, and a revision trigger.
customDeliverableDeclarations.construct: evidence-bounded and revisable policy decision quality
customDeliverableDeclarations.successEvidence: A reader can reconstruct why the decision was made, who bears costs, what is uncertain, and when it must be revisited.
failureConditions: no accountable owner or revision trigger
localDependencies: municipal authority and legal review remain unresolved
customDeliverableDeclarations.accessibilityAndSafety: Use a linear table alternative and never encode affected-group status by color alone.

localConstraints: Do not convert the modeled range into a confidence interval.
Distributional effects cannot be compensated by an aggregate dollar score.
Legal authority is unresolved and requires local verification.
adversarialConditions: Aggregate benefit can hide a non-compensable relocation impact.
